diagram.name: Private Atom Cloud — Cloud Attachment Topology

mxCell.value: Boomi Runtime Cloud Cluster — Cloud Attachment Topology
Generic reference architecture — shows how cloud attachments bind subscriber environments to a shared private runtime cloud cluster
Binds an environment to the cloud cluster
Scoped runtime context with env extensions
Private Runtime Cloud Cluster (Customer-Hosted Infrastructure) (N-number of Clusters)
Shared NFS Mount /boomi/share/cluster (R/W from all nodes)

All nodes share a common NFS-backed installation directory. The head node coordinates scheduling; worker nodes execute integration processes. Multiple subscriber accounts attach via Cloud Attachments — each runs isolated within its own environment context.
Extensions: • DEV API endpoints • DEV credentials • DEV-specific properties
Extensions: • TEST API endpoints • TEST credentials • TEST-specific properties
Extensions: • UAT API endpoints • UAT credentials • UAT-specific properties
Extensions: • PROD API endpoints • PROD credentials • PROD-specific properties

Key Concepts:

 (1) The cloud cluster is a shared runtime — all attached environments execute processes on the same nodes.
 (2) Each Cloud Attachment carries its own environment extensions (connection overrides, credentials, properties), so the same deployed package behaves differently per environment.
 (3) Sub-attachments allow one account to further isolate workloads (e.g., by department or region) within a single environment.
 (4) A Private Runtime Cloud can support multiple Cloud Clusters.
Optional: Sub-Attachments (department / tenant isolation within a single environment)
